description: Creates a SPECTRUM (.ana) from scratch that follows the pitch contour in a binary pitchfile, with a caller-specified harmonic recipe: 'repitch synth binarypitchfile outanalfile harmonics-data'. Arity-0 data-driven entry - the pitchfile rides the pre-output aux slot, the harmonics file rides the positional slot after the output. The harmonics file is a plain list of per-harmonic amplitudes from harmonic 1 upward, CDP-enforced 0-1 each ('ERROR: Partial amplitude[2] = 2.000000 is out of range (0.000000 - 1.000000)' verbatim); an inline number is refused ('Can't open textfile 0.7 to read data.' - file only); 30 harmonics verified accepted. Content verified: synthesizing from a wobbling 261 Hz pitch track yields a resynthesis whose fundamental follows the track (241 Hz mid-file, matching the source's tracked mean). Output duration = the pitchfile's duration (2.0230 from a 2.023 s track). Binary pitchfile only - text pitch data refuses (typed main infile). Tolerates -1/-2 marker values in the pitchfile (a -z-extracted file ran fine). Deterministic (identical data chunks).
musical_use: Melody in, brand-new instrument out: this is CDP's data-to-sound synthesizer - take any tracked pitch (or one composed from scratch via execute() repitch generate from time/MIDI pairs) and give it a fresh harmonic body. The harmonics list IS the timbre: '1' alone = pure sine; 1/n rolloff = sawtooth-ish warmth; odd-harmonics-only (1 0 0.3 0 0.2) = hollow clarinet; a spike at one high harmonic = bell partial. Because the pitch data carries every micro-inflection of the tracked performance, the synthetic voice inherits human phrasing - the classic move is doubling a vocal with a clean harmonic shadow (extract with getpitch 1, synth, mix under the original), or replacing a voice entirely while keeping its melody. For singing vowels instead of a fixed recipe, use repitch vowels. The output is a normal .ana: transpose it, blur it, morph it - or just resynthesize. Chain verified: getpitch 1 -> synth -> pvoc synth, all curated.

pitchfile.description: BINARY pitch data file (.frq) - the pitchdata side file of the curated repitch getpitch 1, or built from scratch via execute(['repitch','generate','out.frq','midiscore.txt','44100']) from time/MIDI pairs. Text pitch data refuses (exit 255, typed infile). Marker values (-1 unpitched / -2 silence) tolerated (verified). Pre-output argv slot; resolves data/ then session root.

harmonics.description: Text file listing the amplitude of each harmonic in sequence from harmonic 1 upward (whitespace/newline separated; write with write_data_file()). Each value CDP-enforced 0-1 ('Partial amplitude[2] = 2.000000 is out of range (0.000000 - 1.000000)' verbatim); 30 harmonics verified. Inline numbers refused ('Can't open textfile 0.7 to read data.'). Renders after the output path.

examples.description: Sawtooth-warm shadow of a tracked vocal.
examples.expected_use:
saw.txt = '1
0.5
0.33
0.25
0.2
' (1/n rolloff). Output .ana sings the tracked melody; resynthesize or layer under the original.

examples.description: Hollow odd-harmonic voice from a composed melody.
examples.expected_use:
melody.frq via execute() repitch generate from time/MIDI pairs; clar.txt = '1
0
0.4
0
0.25
' - clarinet-hollow timbre on your own line.

known_issues: Arity-0 entry: call process() with no input audio - the pitchfile aux is the source of both contour and duration (output = pitchfile's duration; duration_model 'static' evaluates as a skip with no inputs, the watchdog covers reactively).
Binary pitchfile ONLY (text refuses, exit 255) - the necessary text->binary conversion (brktopi) is execute()-only on this build.
Harmonic amplitudes hard-capped 0-1 (verbatim refusal pinned); the harmonics slot takes a FILE only.

Loudness follows the pitch data's amplitude conventions, not the original source's envelope - probe RMS was 0.076; apply envel/gain downstream if you need the original dynamics (repitch analenv extracts the source .ana's window envelope for exactly this).
Unpitched (-1) and silence (-2) markers pass through without refusal; extracted-with--z files synthesize their pitched regions (verified running).
